findings.claim: For the OCR J352 exam, context (AO3) must be embedded within analysis.
findings.truth: The house validator rejects spec codes in lesson text. Say "In the exam".
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT.md banned-string list: spec codes like "OCR J352". Only occurrence in the unit.

findings.claim: Under the heading "The Meryton Ball": "Meanwhile, Mrs Bennet loudly boasts about Jane's prospects, Lydia and Kitty flirt with officers, and Mary performs an embarrassing piano piece."
findings.truth: All three happen at the Netherfield ball (ch.18), not the Meryton assembly (ch.3). The militia only reaches Meryton in ch.7, so no officers are present at the first ball, and Mary does not perform there.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1342: ch.3 (lines 959-1149) has no officers and no Mary performance; ch.18 has "Mary, after very little entreaty, preparing to oblige the company" and Mr Bennet stopping her second song.

findings.claim: Knowledge check stem "Darcy's first proposal begins: 'In _____ I have struggled.'" and flashcard answer "'In vain I have struggled.'"
findings.truth: Austen writes "In vain have I struggled." The lesson content_html already has it right; the question and the flashcard invert the word order. Correct answer stays "vain".
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1342 line 7536 (ch.34): "In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed."

findings.claim: "I am only resolved to act in that manner which will constitute my happiness" (also lesson 7 content_html, and a flashcard in each lesson).
findings.truth: Words are dropped inside the quotation marks with no ellipsis. Austen: "I am only resolved to act in that manner, which will, in my own opinion, constitute my happiness, without reference to you..."

findings.claim: Mr Bennet: "I am heartily ashamed of myself," he admits. Also a flashcard: "Quote Mr Bennet's confession of parental failure." - "'I am heartily ashamed of myself.'"
findings.truth: Fabricated quotation. Mr Bennet never says this. His real admission is "let me once in my life feel how much I have been to blame." The only "heartily ashamed" line in the novel is Darcy's, in ch.58.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1342 line 11224 (ch.48) for Mr Bennet; line 13799 (ch.58) for Darcy. No match anywhere for "ashamed of myself".

findings.claim: "She calls the Bennets 'obstinate, headstrong'", and a flashcard asking what Lady Catherine calls "the Bennet family".
findings.truth: Lady Catherine says it straight to Elizabeth, as "Obstinate, headstrong girl!" It is not said about the family.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1342 line 13354 (ch.56): "Obstinate, headstrong girl! I am ashamed of you!"

findings.claim: Darcy's second proposal is quoted as "an eagerness that had nothing of pride or resentment about it". The phrase also drives a knowledge check (fill), a flashcard answer and the exam tip.
findings.truth: Fabricated quotation - the phrase is not in the novel. The real second proposal reads "You are too generous to trifle with me... My affections and wishes are unchanged; but one word from you will silence me on this subject for ever." The exam tip also quotes "against his will"; Elizabeth's words are "against your will".
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1342 lines 13729-13733 (ch.58); line 7591 (ch.34) for "against your will". No match for "nothing of pride" or that eagerness phrase anywhere in the text.

findings.claim: "pride is justified self-respect, vanity is concern for others' opinion"
findings.truth: Mary's distinction is about whose opinion counts, not about pride being justified: "Pride relates more to our opinion of ourselves; vanity to what we would have others think of us." The lesson's own knowledge check states it correctly, so the key fact contradicts it.

findings.claim: "It assesses AO1, AO2 and AO3." / "This is typically a closed-text exam" / "Check your exam board's specimen paper for the exact format, mark weightings and timing." Key fact: "AO1 = ... AO2 = ... AO3 = ... The examiner wants all three woven together", with a revision tip asking for "the three Assessment Objectives".
findings.truth: AO4 (spelling, punctuation and grammar) IS assessed on the 19th-century prose question - it is the section of the component that carries AO4. Nothing in this unit tells students their writing accuracy is marked. The format is not uncertain either: closed text, 40 marks, one extended response chosen from two (an extract-based question linking to the whole novel, or a discursive question), about an hour.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md section 3h: "Learners will be assessed on the use of a range of vocabulary and sentence structures ... (AO4) in Section B of each examined component. AO4 will carry a 5% weighting." Section 3a for the 80-mark, 2-hour, 40+40 closed-text structure and the choice of two.

findings.claim: Five flashcards answer in a single word under a stem that is not What is / Who was / When / Name: L1 "1813.", L1 "1775-1817.", L2 "Longbourn.", L2 "Five.", L3 "Elizabeth."
findings.truth: Either the stem or the answer has to change. Facts are all correct; only the shape breaks the rule.
findings.evidence: House flashcard rule supplied with this unit's brief.

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions across the 8 lessons are typed "40 marks - Shakespeare Essay".
findings.truth: This is the 19th-century prose question, in the modern and literary heritage component. Shakespeare sits in the other component. Relabelled "40 marks - 19th-century prose essay"; the 40-mark total is correct and is kept.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md section 3a. Same defect as the sibling OCR 19th-century units.

findings.claim: Ladders are malformed. Lessons 1-4 and 6-8 run six rows with "Top band" printed twice (35-40 and 29-34) and a non-house "Lower band". Lesson 5 uses "Band 6:" plus "Lower bands: less balanced."
findings.truth: Rescaled to five equal house bands over the real 40-mark total: Top (33-40), Upper-mid (25-32), Mid (17-24), Lower-mid (9-16), Low (1-8). Each question keeps its own top-band indicative content.
findings.evidence: House ladder vocabulary in CHECK_PROMPT.md; 40 marks confirmed in specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md section 3a.

findings.claim: Lessons 6, 7 and 8 are live with unwritten placeholders: conclusion_html reads "Key point 1. / Key point 2. / Key point 3."; all five glossary_terms read term/definition; and all six practice_questions in each lesson repeat the identical stem "Analyse a key aspect of this section of the novel."
findings.truth: Two options. (a) Author the content now: 3 takeaways + 5 glossary terms + 6 questions per lesson, 18 questions in all - the source paragraphs already supply the terms (narrative voice, dramatic irony, free indirect discourse, comedy of manners for lesson 6; pride, prejudice, reputation for lesson 7). (b) Route it through the standing English Literature placeholder-content item, which Tom has said is fixes-on-approval. I recommend (a) for the conclusions and glossaries, which are unambiguous, and (a) for the questions too - six identical prompts in a row is what a student actually meets. Not edited here because it is authoring, not correction. ORCHESTRATOR: authoring, not a surgical fix; logged for Tom (placeholder content in live L6-L8).
findings.evidence: raw/L06.txt, raw/L07.txt, raw/L08.txt - CONCLUSION_HTML, GLOSSARY_TERMS and PRACTICE_QUESTIONS blocks.

findings.claim: Titles have drifted by one against their content. Lesson 6 "Character Analysis" teaches irony and narrative voice. Lesson 7 "Irony & Narrative Voice" teaches pride, class, marriage and reputation. Lesson 8 "Key Themes & Exam Technique" teaches exam technique only.
findings.truth: Each lesson's description matches its own content, so it is the titles that are wrong. Suggested: 6 = "Irony & Narrative Voice", 7 = "Key Themes", 8 = "Exam Technique". No lesson in the unit covers character analysis, which is what the unit is missing.

summary: Eight lessons checked against Gutenberg #1342 and the OCR J352 specification. Three fabricated or misattributed quotations, all in lesson 5 (a Mr Bennet line that does not exist, Lady Catherine's insult moved from Elizabeth to the family, and an invented description of the second proposal that also drove a knowledge check). Lesson 8 never tells students AO4 is assessed and hedges a format that the spec states plainly. All 48 practice questions were labelled Shakespeare essays with malformed six-row ladders. Every knowledge-check answer key in the unit is correct; no per-AO mark split was invented anywhere; no lesson cites a chapter number, so there is no volume-numbering mismatch. 122 edits written, covering 12 findings; lessons 6-8 also carry unwritten placeholder conclusions, glossaries and practice stems, left for adjudication.
